description: Security & Sandboxing settings page. Configures agent sandboxing policies following the AST 7-layer defense model: compute isolation, resource limits, filesystem boundaries, network mediation, credential proxy, action governance, and audit logging. Supports three built-in profiles (permissive/standard/strict) plus a custom profile editor with full sub-policy configuration.

groups.name: Page Header & Title
groups.description: The page header shows the Shield icon, title 'Security & Sandboxing', and subtitle description.

assertions.description: The page heading 'Security & Sandboxing' is displayed at the top
Subtitle text explains the page purpose: sandbox constraints for workflow execution

groups.name: Security Profile Selector
groups.description: Dropdown to select the active security profile. Options: Permissive, Standard, Strict, Custom. Selecting a built-in profile shows its description and AST fingerprint.

assertions.description: A 'Security Profile' label is visible above the dropdown
A select dropdown with profile options is present. It must include at least Permissive, Standard, Strict, and Custom options.

When a built-in profile is selected (permissive/standard/strict), a description panel appears below the dropdown explaining the profile's posture. The description should mention key features like 'No restrictions' for permissive, 'Balanced' for standard, or 'Maximum isolation' for strict.
assertions.precondition: A built-in profile (not custom) is selected

assertions.description: When a built-in profile is selected, the AST fingerprint notation is displayed in monospace font (e.g., 'L1:2/L2:1/L3:1/L4:0/L5:1/L6:1')

Changing the profile dropdown to 'Standard' updates the description to mention balanced security, credential proxy, and destructive command blocking. The Security Posture visualization bars should also update to show higher scores.

groups.name: Security Posture Visualization
groups.description: A 7-layer bar chart showing the current profile's security scores. Each layer (L1:Compute through L7:Audit) has a colored bar indicating enforcement level: None (red), Cooperative (orange), Software (yellow), Kernel (green).

assertions.description: The 'Security Posture' section heading is visible
All 7 AST layers are listed: L1:Compute, L2:Resources, L3:Filesystem, L4:Network, L5:Credentials, L6:Actions, L7:Audit. Each has a label, colored bar segments, and a score label.
When 'Permissive' profile is selected, the L4:Network layer should show the lowest score (None/0) since permissive mode has no network restrictions. Most other layers should show low scores (1-2).

groups.name: Custom Profile Editor
groups.description: When 'Custom' profile is selected, a full sub-policy editor appears with sections for Network, Actions, Filesystem, Resources, and Credentials. Each section has appropriate form controls.

assertions.description: When the profile dropdown is set to 'Custom', the 'Custom Policy Editor' panel appears with a Sliders icon and sub-sections for Network, Actions, Filesystem, Resources, and Credentials.
The Network section has a Mode dropdown with options: Unrestricted, Allow List, Deny List, Disabled. Selecting 'Allow List' or 'Deny List' reveals a textarea for entering domains (one per line).
The Actions section has a 'Block destructive commands' toggle and a textarea for blocked command regex patterns.
The Resources section shows a 2x2 grid with CPU limit (cores), Memory (MB), PID limit, and Timeout (sec) number inputs.
The Credentials section has a Mode dropdown with options: Direct, Proxy (placeholder injection), Denied (no credentials).

groups.name: Features Section
groups.description: Toggle switches for the three main security features: Credential Proxy, Network Mediation, and Security Audit Log.

assertions.description: The 'Features' section heading is visible
A 'Credential Proxy' toggle is present with description mentioning placeholder injection
A 'Network Mediation' toggle is present with description mentioning domain allowlisting
A 'Security Audit Log' toggle is present with description mentioning policy decisions
When the audit log toggle is enabled, an 'Audit Retention (days)' number input appears with a left border indent. Default value should be 30.
assertions.precondition: Security Audit Log toggle is enabled

groups.name: Audit Log Viewer
groups.description: When audit logging is enabled, a scrollable table shows recent security audit events with summary badges, filter dropdown, refresh button, and JSON export button.

assertions.description: When audit logging is enabled, the 'Audit Log' panel appears with a FileSearch icon, heading, and summary badges showing allowed/denied/warning counts.
assertions.precondition: Security Audit Log toggle is enabled

assertions.description: A filter dropdown with options All, Denied, Allowed, Warnings is present in the audit log header
The audit event table has 5 columns: Time, Type, Decision, Action, Reason. Column headers are visible when events are loaded.
Each audit event row shows a colored decision badge: green for 'allowed', red for 'denied', yellow for 'warning'. The type column shows a label badge (e.g., 'Network', 'Command', 'Policy').
assertions.precondition: Audit events are loaded and visible

assertions.description: When no audit events exist, the table area shows 'No audit events. Click refresh to load.' message
assertions.precondition: Audit logging is enabled but no events loaded yet

assertions.description: When audit events are loaded, a download button appears in the audit header. Clicking it exports the events as a JSON file with filename format 'security-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.json'.

groups.name: AST 7-Layer Info Banner
groups.description: An informational banner explaining the Agent Sandbox Taxonomy (AST) 7-layer model at the bottom of the page.

assertions.description: A blue-tinted info banner mentions 'Agent Sandbox Taxonomy (AST)' and lists all 7 layers: L1:Compute, L2:Resources, L3:Filesystem, L4:Network, L5:Credentials, L6:Actions, L7:Audit

groups.name: Action Buttons
groups.description: Reset to Defaults and Save Security Settings buttons at the bottom of the page.

assertions.description: A 'Reset to Defaults' button is present with neutral styling
A 'Save Security Settings' button is present with blue/primary styling and a Shield icon

Clicking 'Save Security Settings' shows a spinner while saving, then shows 'Saved' with a check icon on success. A green 'Settings saved' toast appears. On error, a red error banner appears at the top.
Clicking 'Reset to Defaults' resets the profile to 'permissive', disables all feature toggles (credential proxy, network mediation, audit log), and clears any custom policy.

groups.name: Visual Design & Typography
groups.description: Dark theme styling with neutral-800 card backgrounds, blue-400 accents, and consistent text hierarchy.

assertions.description: All settings cards use a dark semi-transparent background (bg-neutral-800/50) with subtle border (border-neutral-700/50) and rounded corners (rounded-lg).

Page title uses text-lg font-semibold text-white. Section headings use text-sm font-medium text-neutral-200. Sub-labels use text-xs text-neutral-300 or text-neutral-400. Description text uses text-[10px] text-neutral-500.
Toggle switches use blue-600 when enabled and neutral-600 when disabled. The toggle knob is white and transitions smoothly.
The Save button uses bg-blue-600 with white text. The Reset button uses bg-neutral-700 with neutral-200 text. Both have hover states.

groups.name: Loading & Error States
groups.description: The page handles loading, error, and success states appropriately.

assertions.description: While settings are loading, a centered 'Loading security settings...' message is displayed instead of the form.
When a settings operation fails, a red error banner appears at the top showing the error message with red-400 text on red-500/10 background.
assertions.precondition: A save or load operation has failed

assertions.description: After successful save, a green 'Settings saved' banner appears with a Check icon. It auto-dismisses after 3 seconds.
